html:
Mayas marks the Maya of the Yucatán Peninsula in the 1500s, during and after the Spanish conquest. After the fall of Mayapán in the mid-1400s, northern Yucatán was split into some sixteen rival provinces, each under its own lords, heirs of the Maya city-states.

The Montejo family led the conquest from 1527. Early campaigns failed, but in 1542 the Spanish founded Mérida on the ruins of the Maya city of T'ho, and by 1546 they had crushed a great revolt in the east. The Itza of Tayasal, in the forests of Petén to the south, held out until 1697.

The Franciscan friar Diego de Landa ran a harsh campaign against Maya religion; in 1562 at Maní he burned Maya books, of which only a few, such as the Dresden Codex, survive. His own account later helped scholars read the Maya script. The Yucatec Maya language is still spoken by hundreds of thousands. See also Maya (Yucateco).
